history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: His family is put with the village on the Little Calumet, on the Little Calumet, about five leagues from Chicago (about a hundred men in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Fox gens (Wake-shĭ′), and his children are of it after him.
He has seen the French and the English traders come and go, and the Americans build the fort in 1803.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

He is of the Wolf gens (Mo-ăh′), and his children are of it after him.
The winter before, he hunted with his family on the Kankakee and traded the skins at Kinzie's for powder, cloth and kettles.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: Her family is put with the village on the Little Calumet, on the Little Calumet, about five leagues from Chicago (about a hundred men in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
She is of the Black Hawk gens (M′-ke-tash′-she-kă-kah′); her husband, since no one married within the gens, is of another, and her children are of his.
She planted and hoed the village's corn, beans and squash in the spring, and made the rush and cattail mats the lodges here are covered with.
She came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: Her family is put with the village on the Little Calumet, on the Little Calumet, about five leagues from Chicago (about a hundred men in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
She is of the Turkey gens (Pen′-nă, as Morgan writes it), her father's, and her name is a name of childhood, to be put aside for another as she grows up.
This summer is the first time this child has seen the fort, the soldiers and so many lodges in one place.

card_evidence.claim: The wigwams along the creek, seen from the fort on the last day.
